brief: Goldman Sachs forecasts August core CPI at 0.23% month over month against 0.2% consensus, a 2.40% year over year rate, and headline CPI at 0.39% against 0.4% consensus, with headline lifted by food at 0.25% and energy at 2.3% as retail gasoline prices rebound. That takes headline year over year to 3.40% from 3.36% in July. Three components drive the core forecast. Autos are mixed: used car prices rise 0.5% on auction price signals, new car prices rise 0.1% as dealer incentives are offset by positive residual seasonality, and auto insurance falls 0.2% on lower premiums in Goldman's online dataset. Shelter stays benign, with owners' equivalent rent at 0.22% and rent at 0.23%, reflecting continued slowdown in underlying trends. Airfares rise 4.0% on jet fuel passthrough from the oil rebound. The same component set maps to a 0.22% core PCE increase, and PPI on Thursday precedes CPI on Friday, giving an incomplete early read. Beyond August, Goldman expects roughly 0.2% monthly core prints for the next couple of months on shelter slowdown and shrinking tariff contributions, with upside risk if oil disruptions persist.
